content: Nelfinavir can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Nelfinavir increases the levels of vemurafenib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, vemurafenib increases nelfinavir levels via the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Nelfinavir elevates the levels or effects of verapamil by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Verapamil, in turn, increases nelfinavir levels through the same pathway and also via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate (inhaled) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of warfarin through mechanisms involving other pathways. Caution and monitoring are necessary. The less potent R-enantiomer of warfarin is partially metabolized by CYP3A4 (as well as CYP1A2 and CYP2C19). INR should be monitored more frequently when coadministered with inhibitors of these isoenzymes, and warfarin dosage should be adjusted as needed. Zafirlukast increases nelfinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Zanubrutinib, a CYP3A4 substrate, should be reduced to 80 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. Nelfinavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Nelfinavir increases zileuton levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The zuranolone dose should be reduced when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Acetazolamide increases nelfinavir levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Nelfinavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, abemaciclib should be increased to the dose prior to initiating the inhibitor. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of acalabrutinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. Nelfinavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. New-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided until adagrasib concentrations have reached steady-state (after ~8 days). If steady-state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and the risk of its toxicities. Nelfinavir increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. DM1, the cytotoxic component, is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. Nelfinavir increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Nelfinavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated.
